subjects.authored_statement: A Before claim containing an explicit Markdown code selector maps that selector only against the canonical base-side changed structural identity.
An After claim containing an explicit Markdown code selector maps that selector only against the canonical head-side changed structural identity.
A successfully matched selector produces the same canonical T/CC structural focus behavior as other eligible transformation claims.
A selector that does not match remains explicitly unassociated rather than silently falling back to lexical or model inference.
Before and After prose without an explicit selector remains structurally not applicable.
Do not let presentation code infer or reconstruct claim-to-graph semantics.
Do not change graph membership, formal assessment authority, or LLM behavior.
Preserve revision-side direction: base-only evidence cannot satisfy After and head-only evidence cannot satisfy Before.
Natural-language semantic guessing, LLM-assisted mapping, and changes to structural graph collection.

The semantic parser classified Before and After as typed state context, then skipped predicate extraction for both kinds. The structural disposition therefore labeled every such T row not applicable, even when the author named an exact file or symbol in a Markdown code span. The renderer correctly consumed the empty overlay, so presentation could not recover the missing mapping.
explicit selectors in Before produce present_base predicates;
explicit selectors in After produce present_head predicates;
canonical subject selection resolves those predicates only against changed structural identities on the declared revision;
the existing bounded closure and projection pipeline produces T focus overlays consumed by the HTML graph;
selector-free state prose remains structurally not applicable;
state assessment remains unverified context, with predicate assessments preserved only to satisfy the canonical contract and explain that structural focus is not proof.
